Recovery and bias-aware precision of back-calculated standards

Source: R/point_estimates_contract.R
standard_recovery.Rd

For calibrators, whose nominal concentration is known, computes the recovery (estimated / nominal, in percent) and the CV of the root-mean-square error, which adds the bias against the nominal value to the standard error: sqrt(se^2 + bias^2) on the log10 scale, expressed as a CV in percent the same way pcov is, and capped at cv_x_max.

Usage

standard_recovery(
  predicted,
  nominal,
  se,
  is_log_independent = TRUE,
  cv_x_max = 150
)

Arguments

predicted

Back-calculated concentration on the fit's x scale (predicted_concentration).

nominal

Nominal concentration on the same scale (the x value the fit used: log10 when is_log_independent).

se

Standard error of predicted, same scale (se_concentration).

is_log_independent

Logical: is x on the log10 scale?

cv_x_max

Cap for the CV, as for pcov (default 150).

Value

A data frame with recovery_pct and pcov_rmse, one row per point. Both are NA where the estimate or the nominal value is missing; a point with an estimate but no finite se gets pcov_rmse = cv_x_max.

Examples

standard_recovery(predicted = c(1.02, 2.10), nominal = c(1, 2), se = c(0.03, 0.05))
#>   recovery_pct pcov_rmse
#> 1     104.7129  8.302089
#> 2     125.8925 25.743684
